solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former pupil, retainer, watchful

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a retainer is a household servant

explanation.surface: A list of three ways to describe an old schoolboy now in service, keeping a careful eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a list of three descriptions, but the first two build the answer and only the last defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone watchful notices what goes on around them, which is the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Getting on, love large service of food

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a dish is a portion of food served up

explanation.surface: An ageing romantic enjoying a big meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Somebody getting on in years is fairly old, somewhat advanced in age.

clue.text: Urbane, put money aside to cover university

indicators.note: to cover means the savings word wraps around the letter for university

parts.note: to save is to put money aside

explanation.surface: A sophisticated person saving up to pay for college.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave and urbane both describe someone smoothly polished and charming in manner.

clue.text: Wine series linguist embraces

indicators.note: embraces says the phrase series linguist holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A language expert hugging a run of bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape and the wine made from it, chiefly German.

clue.text: Confused notice at canal, or the pond

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of notice at canal are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a sign at a canal, or perhaps a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pond' is humorous British and American slang for this ocean, separating the two countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Speakers on both sides jokingly call the ocean between Britain and North America the pond.

clue.text: Initially tense, hesitant and wary, become more relaxed

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Someone at first tense, unsure and cautious gradually loosens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations thaw when they become warmer and friendlier, as ice melts.

clue.text: Regularly upbeat, much-liked

indicators.note: regularly tells us to take every other letter of the word upbeat, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Someone who is reliably cheerful tends to be popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite person or thing, much-liked by others, is called a pet, as in teacher's pet.

clue.text: Opening excerpt

definitions.meaning: an opening or way through, such as a corridor or channel
a short extract from a book or piece of music

explanation.surface: The first extract of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is both a way through and a section quoted from a written work.

clue.text: Story about no good muddle

indicators.note: about means the story word goes round the letters for no good

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A worthless story that is a confused mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a confused, knotted mess, a muddle of string or of affairs.

clue.text: Duck famous navigator

definitions.meaning: a male duck has its own name
Sir Francis ..., the Elizabethan sailor who circumnavigated the globe

explanation.surface: A duck named after a celebrated seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: The male duck is a drake, and Francis Drake was the English explorer who sailed round the world.

clue.text: Worry, after backing one child's contact

indicators.note: backing means the word for worry is read backwards before the other pieces follow

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or worry someone
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a child; the 's is just the possessive joining it to the definition

explanation.surface: Fretting after supporting one's child's acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a working link or connection between people, which is what a contact provides.

clue.text: Doctor sent girl, reliable

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic sent a dependable young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, the subject of 'sent', but it is a verb telling you to rearrange SENT and GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling describes something of solid, dependable quality, like sterling work or a sterling friend.

clue.text: Run away from fight and cry noisily

indicators.note: away from tells us one piece leaves the word for a fight

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone flees a scrap and weeps loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to wail or howl loudly, as a crying baby does.

clue.text: Show at Erskine displaying leisure equipment

indicators.note: displaying says the words Show at Erskine show the answer inside them

explanation.surface: An exhibition at Erskine, a Scottish town, showing off recreational gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A long board worn to skim over water behind a boat is kit for a leisure sport.

clue.text: Group, dynastic, needing reform, obsolete ultimately

indicators.note: something needing reform must be reshaped, so the letters of dynastic are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of obsolete

explanation.surface: A dynastic group that is out of date and in need of reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is an association of people or firms combining for a shared business purpose.

clue.text: Spanish man clutching at politician?

indicators.note: clutching means the Spanish title holds the word at within it

parts.note: señor is Spanish for a man or Mr

explanation.surface: A Spaniard grabbing hold of a statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: a senator is one kind of politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an example of an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: Immature depiction of everyone in Jersey, say?

indicators.note: in says the word for everyone sits inside the cattle word

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, so this is an example
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A childish portrait of the whole population of the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests the Channel Island, but here it is the breed of cow; 'depiction of' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow means inexperienced and lacking adult judgement, like a callow youth.

clue.text: Delicious drink close by impressing court

indicators.note: impressing means the court abbreviation is pressed into the word for close by

parts.note: near means close by

explanation.surface: A tasty drink found close to a court, making an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods and now means any delicious beverage.

clue.text: This relation's gibe, not the first

definitions.note: read as 'this relation is', the definition followed by the link

indicators.note: not the first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for gibe

parts.note: a taunt is a jeering remark, a gibe

explanation.surface: A jibe from this family member, and not for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: Your father's or mother's sister is a family relation of that title.

clue.text: Feature of website game — hope for shake-up

indicators.note: a shake-up is a reorganisation, so the letters of game and hope are rearranged

explanation.surface: A website's games page, hoping for an overhaul.
explanation.definitionFit: The landing page a site opens on is one of its standard features.

clue.text: Foreign article about position of golfer's ball

indicators.note: about says the article goes round the golf word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
in golf the lie is where the ball comes to rest

explanation.surface: An overseas article on where a golfer's ball has landed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means strange or belonging to another country.

clue.text: Rising slander over penny tip

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the next
rising in a down clue means the slander word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: mud, as in mudslinging, is slander

explanation.surface: An upward trend in slander outweighing a small tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity worth a penny, but it is a rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip in British English is a rubbish heap, the same as a dump.

clue.text: Plant leased before truce? Not right

indicators.note: before places the word for leased ahead of the next piece

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for right is removed from truce

explanation.surface: A factory rented out ahead of a ceasefire, but not the right one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory being leased, but it is the vegetable sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad vegetable grown for its leaves is a plant in the garden sense.

clue.text: Family in street with no money

indicators.note: in tells us the family word goes inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: kin are one's relatives, one's family

explanation.surface: A family living on the street because they are penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is informal British slang for being broke, completely out of cash.

clue.text: Coming back unprepared for conflict

indicators.note: coming back means the word for unprepared is read backwards

parts.note: raw can mean untrained or not ready, as a raw recruit

explanation.surface: A soldier returning from fighting he was not ready for.
explanation.definitionFit: A war is armed conflict between nations or groups.

clue.text: Pioneer somehow crossing Poles — he may get income for life

definitions.text: he may get income for life

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged letters span either side of the two poles
somehow says the letters of pioneer are arranged in some other way

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A polar explorer crossing between the Poles, who may be set up for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pioneer' and 'Poles' suggest a polar explorer, but 'Pioneer' is anagram fodder; 'crossing' puts NS inside its rearrangement PEIONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person drawing a state or company pension receives regular payments for the rest of their life.
